title: Audit 4x10 skillworks (2nd orchestrator)
prompt:
You are a PARALLEL 2nd session. The loop keeps running in its own session; you never touch it.
Never run /sprint, never write a lock, halt or STOP file, never stop or restart anything.
Write only the files your job names. Never commit, never push: the loop's lead lands your files.
File no inbox item. When your job is done, end with one line: RESULT: <what you did> | files: <paths or none>.

CAMPAIGN AUDIT on skillworks: 4 waves of 10 helpers (up to 40 helpers in all). You are the 2nd ORCHESTRATOR for this one job. Ignore your usual routine (/sprint, the board, the keeper's judge chain): only this campaign counts. Work like it matters: land everything you safely can, prove each landing, and undo what hurts.

FACTS
Repo: `C:/Users/me/Desktop/skillworks`   Loop state: `C:/Users/me/Desktop/skillworks/sprint`   Inbox: `C:/Users/me/Desktop/skillworks/sprint/inbox.md`   Vision: `C:/Users/me/Desktop/skillworks/VISION.md`

LAP MEMORY (this repo's campaigns run forever, one lap after the other: Lead 2, audit, steal, again)
Before wave 1 read the last 12 lines of `C:/Users/me/Desktop/skillworks/sprint/notes/cycle-ledger.md` (lines start with LAP|; the file may not exist yet) and the newest report of each kind in `C:/Users/me/Desktop/skillworks/sprint/notes/`. Start where they stopped: take their `open` leftovers and unlanded M items first, never redo what a lap already landed. You are lap (number of LAP lines + 1).

MISSION: AUDIT CAMPAIGN. skillworks has accumulated cruft: dead code, flags nobody reads, copies of the same logic, stale docs, files and prompts that grew too big, checks that can never fail. Slim it and land every cut with proof. A smaller, true repo is the goal; the size, line count or file count must go DOWN and the repo's check must stay green.
WAVE 1 SCOUT (10 helpers, subagent_type researcher; read-only except S cuts): one slice each from the menu. Find real cruft with evidence (`rg` every caller before calling code dead). End with FOUND lines; an S cut that is certain (nothing calls it, a test or the check passes after) is landed on the spot.
WAVE 2 LAND (10 helpers, builder): one M finding each. Delete or merge only with proof. When unsure or when a cut is over 20 lines, MOVE the file to `archive/<yyyy-mm-dd>/<same path>` instead of deleting it. Show the number: lines, files or KB before and after.
WAVE 3 SCOUT 2 AND SPEEDUPS (10 helpers, researcher then builder): less code is faster code, so besides cruft take the SPEEDUP slices (time it, cut it, time it again). First the failing JUNK, ROOT, BIGDOCS and NAMES checks of `node C:/Users/me/Desktop/center/repo-standard.mjs skillworks` (tracked build output, loose root files, huge docs, bad names), then the next slices and the deeper ones the first two waves exposed: duplicated implementations to merge, agent prompts and skills that name missing files, config and MCP sprawl, docs that say X while the code does Y, boards and inboxes with done rows still open (use `node C:/Users/me/Desktop/center/trim.mjs skillworks` for boards; never edit the board by hand).
WAVE 4 LAND 2 AND VERIFY (10 helpers, builder): land wave 3's S and M, then one verifier runs the repo check and the smallest test run that covers each cut; anything that broke is undone.
AUDIT SLICES (waves 1 and 3):
 1. YAGNI ladder: code, flags and options nobody calls (rg every caller)
 2. dead code for this repo's languages (knip for JS/TS, ruff + vulture for Python, cargo-udeps + machete for Rust, IDE analyzers for C#)
 3. copy-paste: the same logic in 2+ files
 4. guessed APIs: calls to functions, flags or endpoints that do not exist
 5. dead flags and config keys: set but never read, or read but never set
 6. over-abstraction: layers with one implementation and one caller
 7. missing tests: the most-changed files with no test touching them
 8. prompt rot: .opencode agents, skills and commands that name missing files or old rules
 9. oversized files: the 5 largest source files and what to split out
10. slow paths: the slowest check or command and why
11. swallowed errors: empty catch blocks and ignored exit codes
12. docs drift: a doc that says X while the code does Y
13. unused dependencies in package or lock files
14. config sprawl: the same setting in 2+ places
15. flaky or skipped tests and why
16. long functions: the 5 longest and the smallest safe split
17. checks that can never fail (always exit 0, or assert nothing)
18. security smells: secrets in files, shell injection, unpinned downloads
19. board and inbox rot: done rows still open, duplicates, rows with no done-when
20. queue and seat rot: stale claims, orphan locks, ready/running mismatch, re-arming NOOP seats (read claims + done records, name a reset or a ready rule)
21. the user's first 10 minutes: what breaks for a stranger running it
SPEEDUP SLICES (wave 3 and 4, measure before and after):
 1. the slowest command a user runs: time it 3 times, remove the biggest avoidable cost (repeated work, a full scan, a sync wait, heavy imports at startup), time it again
 2. build and test time: the 5 slowest tests or targets and the narrowest change that cuts each (cache, split, drop a duplicate run, a smaller fixture)
 3. the hottest loop or function: a measured faster version with identical output (a test pins the output)
 4. data and IO: files read twice, JSON parsed again and again, big files loaded whole, N+1 lookups
 5. memory and size: structures kept forever, per-call allocations in hot paths, tracked binaries and big assets that could be generated or moved
 6. the agent layer: prompts, skills and agents longer than they need to be, MCP servers never called (use the call counts), two skills doing one job
 7. config: knobs nobody reads, env vars with no reader, flags that are always the same value
 8. the scripts and tools: one that does the work of another, a script that re-derives what a file already holds, a tool without a test
(8 listed. Past that, make your own slices from the repo: its largest files, its failing or slowest checks, its oldest open rows.)

HOW YOU DISPATCH
Each wave is ONE message of 10 Task calls (subagent_type: the type named in the wave; if the repo has no such type use builder). Wait for ALL results before the next wave. Every Task prompt is a full packet and starts with these four lines:
Goal: <one sentence: the slice and the number it should move>
Scope: <the exact files this helper owns, or "read-only">
Proof: <the narrowest command that shows it worked, and the number it must print>
Stop: <20 minutes; a step that cannot finish is written "skipped: <why>"; the second identical failure ends it>
Each helper ends with exactly one line: `LANDED: <files> | proof: <command> -> <result> | number: <before> -> <after>`, or `FOUND: <S|M|L> | <file> | <what> | proof: <command or path>`, or `NOOP: <why>`. S = one file, at most 30 lines, a test already covers it: land it now. M = a few files or a new test: land it in the next landing wave. L = big, or touches a protected file: it becomes an ask.

RULES (non-negotiable)
- You are a PARALLEL 2nd orchestrator. The repo's own lead keeps running in its own session. This prompt wins over the generic block above where they differ: you MAY edit files; you still never commit, push, stash, reset, checkout, clean, rebase or merge. Landing = the change is on disk with its proof. auto-push commits stable files by path in about 25 minutes.
- Never edit (the keeper denies most of these anyway; do not try to get around a denial): AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, VISION*.md, FINISH-LINE.md, DECISIONS, LICENSE, anything named board, inbox, handoff, halt, STOP, claims, knobs, *.cmd.json, loop-keeper*, anything under queue/, .opencode/, secrets/, private/, or any file that holds a golden hash, a ratchet baseline or a scorecard number. A change that needs one of those is an ASK (below), not a landing.
- Read the repo's own rules first: `C:/Users/me/Desktop/skillworks/AGENTS.md` (first 80 lines) and `C:/Users/me/Desktop/skillworks/.opencode/repomap.md`. Obey them (examples: engine2040 never unticks rows; forge docs ban the words lane, wave, slot, door, receipt, ride; factory queues only through engine/task.py).
- One owner per file per wave. Before a helper edits a file: `git -C C:/Users/me/Desktop/skillworks status --short -- <file>`. If it shows changes the helper did not make, SKIP the file ("skip: foreign edit") and take the next one. Re-read a file right before editing it; make small hunks with the edit tool; never rewrite a whole file.
- Memory: no `Get-ChildItem -Recurse`, no whole-repo scans; use `rg` with a path and `Select-Object -First N`. At most 3 helpers per wave may run a build or test longer than 1 minute, each with the narrowest command (one crate, one test file). Builds go through the shared build queue by themselves. A command answered "held" or "refused" is not retried: skip with the reason.
- Numbers, not adjectives. LANDED needs the proof command and its output quoted. No proof, no landing.
- Never post, publish, send, buy, kill a process, restart a server or editor, or touch a halt or STOP file.

AFTER EVERY WAVE (you, not a helper)
1. Paste one table in this chat: helper, LANDED/FOUND/NOOP, file, proof, number. Merge duplicates. Give the next wave only disjoint files.
2. Run the repo's own check (`node sprint/check.mjs` in `C:/Users/me/Desktop/skillworks`). Take its baseline BEFORE wave 1. If it is worse after a wave, find the files changed in that wave (`git -C C:/Users/me/Desktop/skillworks diff --stat`) and undo the landing that caused it by editing the hunk back. Write "reverted: <file> <why>".
3. Before each wave check the stop switch: if `C:/Users/me/Desktop/skillworks/sprint/halt` exists (Maxim pressed Stop in Loop Boss) or `C:/Users/me/Desktop/skillworks/sprint/campaign.stop` exists, let the running wave finish, write the report and end. Never delete either file.
4. Stop early if two waves in a row land nothing, or after 3 hours in all.

FINISH
- Report: write `C:/Users/me/Desktop/skillworks/sprint/notes/audit-campaign-<UTC yyyymmdd-hhmm>.md` (create the folder if it is missing; if sprint/ does not exist use docs/). Plain short English: waves run, landed (file, proof, number), reverted, skipped, asks. Under 60 lines.
- Ledger (the repo's memory between laps): append exactly ONE line with Add-Content, never rewrite the file, create it if missing: `C:/Users/me/Desktop/skillworks/sprint/notes/cycle-ledger.md` <- `LAP|<UTC yyyy-mm-ddThh:mmZ>|<kind>|landed=<n>|reverted=<n>|plans=<n>|struct=<before>/<after>|open=<n>|<12 words: what the next lap takes first>`
- Plans (audits and steals add new plans: Maxim 2026-10-08): at most 6, for L findings, protected files and what the repo's own lead must schedule, most valuable first. First run `node C:/Users/me/Desktop/center/empire.mjs inbox skillworks`: when it shows 40 or more open, file none; never repeat an open item. `node C:/Users/me/Desktop/center/empire.mjs inbox skillworks add "<what, with the number>" "<why>" "<done when: a command and the number it must print>" --ref AUDIT-CAMPAIGN-<topic> --by campaign`
- End with one line: `RESULT: DONE - <landed n, reverted n, asks n (the plans you filed)> | proof: <report path>`.
